title: The Divine Council
lead: Several passages picture God presiding over a court of heavenly beings, called "sons of God," "holy ones" or even "gods" (Psalm 82:1; 1 Kings 22:19–22; Job 1:6). Deuteronomy 32:8–9 may say that God set the nations under these beings while keeping Israel for himself. Scholars debate how this fits with the Bible's claim that the LORD alone is God. This page is about the heavenly court around God; for the "sons of God" who take human wives in Genesis 6, see the page on fallen angels.

sections.h: The council in the Old Testament
sections.b: The prophet Micaiah sees the LORD on his throne with "all the army of heaven" standing beside him, debating how to lure King Ahab to his death (1 Kings 22:19–22). In Job the "sons of God" come to present themselves before the LORD, and the accuser comes with them (Job 1:6; Job 2:1). Psalm 82 has God standing "in the council of God" and judging "gods" who have ruled the nations unjustly, then sentencing them to die like humans. Isaiah overhears the council and volunteers (Isaiah 6:8), and Daniel's "watchers" and "holy ones" issue decrees (Daniel 4:17). Many scholars connect these scenes with the assembly of the gods under El in the Ugaritic texts from Syria (about 1300 BC); others stress how the Bible reduces these beings to servants of the one God.
